summary: On node1, created the datauser account and a dedicated 1 GiB loopback XFS filesystem mounted at /srv/data (via /etc/fstab, persistent), owned by datauser, with an XFS user quota of 100MB (bsoft=bhard=100m) set for datauser. Enforcement was verified by the kernel itself: a 150MB write as datauser was truncated to exactly 100M with "Disk quota exceeded", while a 10MB write succeeded. Performed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id/mount/quota/data, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until exec was available again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified the mount, quota configuration, existing data, and quota enforcement (repeat 150MB write again failed at 100MB) all survived and function correctly post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/filesystem/disk layout and confirmed no pre-existing datauser or /srv/data mount
Created 1GiB backing image, formatted XFS, added persistent fstab entry with uquota,prjquota,loop options, mounted at /srv/data, chowned to datauser
Set XFS user quota bsoft=bhard=100m for datauser on /srv/data
Verified enforcement pre-reboot: 150MB write failed with Disk quota exceeded at exactly 100MB; 10MB write succeeded
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, mount state, quota report, data listing
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 (single node, async so ack returned)
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed from 06339ff3-9f53-4e1d-9bf4-1210144ee001 to 964e471a-aab6-4428-8b06-3676123a3533, proving actual restart

Re-verified post-reboot: /srv/data mount persisted with usrquota,prjquota options, quota config intact, prior data (smallfile) intact, and quota enforcement re-confirmed by another 150MB write failing at 100MB

evidence.requirement: datauser account exists and 100MB filesystem-enforced quota configured under /srv/data
evidence.summary: Initial state showed no datauser/no /srv/data mount; second command created datauser, built dedicated XFS loop mount at /srv/data, and set xfs_quota user limit bsoft=bhard=100m for datauser

evidence.requirement: Quota is enforced by the filesystem itself (kernel-level), not a soft/script check
evidence.summary: dd write of 150MB as datauser was cut off by the kernel at exactly 100M with 'Disk quota exceeded'; a 10MB write succeeded and quota report reflected usage
Captured boot_id 06339ff3-9f53-4e1d-9bf4-1210144ee001, confirmed /srv/data mounted with usrquota,prjquota, quota report showing datauser at 10M/100M, and smallfile present
systemctl reboot issued in background; command returned 'reboot issued' successfully before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity, not just elapsed time
evidence.summary: Connection timed out/reset during reboot window, then exec succeeded again returning new boot_id 964e471a-aab6-4428-8b06-3676123a3533, differing from baseline, with uptime reset to 0 minutes

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data and re-verified quota enforcement
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data remained mounted with usrquota,prjquota options, quota config and prior data (smallfile) intact, and a repeat 150MB write as datauser again failed at exactly 100MB with Disk quota exceeded
